title: Robots That Must Not Deadlock: Warehouse Fleet Reservation Discipline
strategies: trivial: only robot 0 works, one order per trip, never charges, all other robots idle -> matches the evaluator's own weak reference exactly

greedy: every robot works, but round-robins orders one-at-a-time (no batching), never schedules a charging detour, and resolves priority by plain robot index -- the obvious 'independent shortest path per robot' recipe. Fine on the low-density instances (little aisle contention, battery never gets close to empty) but collapses on the high-density trap instances: single-order trips flood the shared single-lane corridor, queuing cascades eat the horizon, and batteries run dry with no charging stops budgeted, permanently stranding robots mid-shift

strong: a discrete-event dispatcher that batches up to K currently-released orders per round trip (nearest-shelf-first, sweeping outward once instead of round-tripping per order -- far fewer aisle-edge crossings), and proactively detours to recharge (to full) before a trip that would run the battery dry rather than after stranding -- a genuine reservation discipline that costs individual robots time (charging detours) to raise fleet throughput
invalid: priority list is not a permutation of 0..R-1 (duplicate index) -- rejected on every instance
